dossier.public_summary: The dip is exactly at the star's 0.74-day spin period and varies much more from 21000 to 14000 ppm spot signal than a transit explains. The transit depth changes by ~57% between sectors and the star's phase curve is almost as strong as the dip itself. With no nearby star able to mimic it, the best explanation is stellar activity/variability, not a 2.9-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Very large phase-curve swing almost equal to the 5143 ppm dip depth with high chi2 indicates stellar variability/binary modulation, not a planet transit signal.
Dip period is essentially identical to the stellar rotation period (1x multiple) with extremely significant spot modulation in both sectors, favouring spots/pulsation at spin period over a planet.
